title: Christmas Comes Early For The US Consumer
gist: Gavekal argues the post-Covid K-shaped US economy is unwinding: asset-poor consumers squeezed by a soft labor market, high energy prices, borrowing costs and Trump's immigration policies now benefit from a tighter labor market and Democratic midterm gains pointing to cheaper fuel and softer immigration policy. It is constructive on the ordinary US consumer and consumer stocks, with a stalling AI capex engine the main risk.

themes.theme: End of the K-shaped US consumer

insights.claim: Gavekal argues that despite recent turmoil in the US equity market, the outlook is improving for the ordinary US consumer and for US consumer stocks.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Broad-based US consumer discretionary exposure may be worth adding even amid equity volatility, not just high-end names.
insights.quote: things are looking up for the ordinary US consumer, and for US consumer stocks

insights.claim: In the post-Covid US 'K-shaped' economy, asset-rich households kept spending despite moderating income growth because rising equity portfolio values supported them (a wealth effect), while asset-poor consumers were squeezed by a soft labor market, higher energy prices, inflation and higher borrowing costs.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Consumer spending has been hostage to equity prices; a shift in support to the asset-poor cohort reduces that dependence.
insights.quote: Untroubled by moderating income growth, asset-rich households continued to spend, encouraged by the rising value of their equity portfolios.

insights.claim: Donald Trump's strict immigration policies compounded the squeeze on lower-income US consumers, as consumer businesses serving immigrant communities saw their client bases shrink.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Businesses with immigrant-heavy customer bases were a hidden casualty and are candidates for recovery if policy softens.
insights.quote: consumer businesses serving immigrant communities saw their client bases shrink

insights.claim: Gavekal says the US labor market has tightened, reversing one of the headwinds that squeezed asset-poor consumers.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tighter labor markets support wage-driven spending by lower-income households.

insights.claim: Gavekal reads the Democratic Party's gains in the November 2026 US midterm elections as pointing to cheaper gasoline and diesel prices and a less severe stance on immigration, both of which would relieve lower-income consumers.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Lower pump prices and softer immigration enforcement act as a real-income boost for mass-market consumer businesses.
insights.quote: the Democratic Party’s gains in last Tuesday’s midterm elections point to cheaper pump prices for gasoline and diesel, as well as a less severe stance on immigration

insights.claim: Gavekal concludes that the headwinds that held back a large portion of the US consumer market now appear to be fading, though sizable risks remain, notably that the US AI capital-expenditure engine could stall.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: An AI capex stall is the key risk to watch for the consumer-recovery call, since it could hit both equities and labor demand.
insights.quote: There remain sizable risks, including the possibility that the US AI capex engine could stall.
